info.title: Biohub Local CV Pack: Folds, GT Stats, Scorer
info.subtitle: Prefix-holdout folds, per-volume GT stats, scorer harness, board timeline
info.description:
# Biohub Local CV Pack: Folds, GT Stats, Scorer

Everything you need to validate a Biohub cell-tracking pipeline locally instead of reading the public leaderboard: a fixed two-fold prefix-holdout split over all 195 clean train volumes, per-volume ground-truth statistics, the local scoring harness for the competition's own `tracking_cellmot` metric, per-volume behavior of a public 0.915-class fork pipeline, and a dated public-leaderboard snapshot plus timeline showing why local validation is the only measurement that predicts anything.

## Why this exists

The four public test volumes of `biohub-cell-tracking-during-development` are train twins: `44b6_0113de3b`, `44b6_0b24845f`, `6bba_05b6850b`, `6bba_05db0fb1`. The public leaderboard therefore rewards memorization, ~243 teams share a displayed 0.915 from one fork lineage (ranks 332–574 on 2026-08-20 — entirely below the bronze line at rank 258, displayed 0.917), and Kaggle displays 3 decimals while ranking on full precision. A rank inside that block is a queue position, not a result. If you want a number that survives private scoring, you need local validation on volumes your pipeline has never seen — that is what this pack provides.

## Files

- `folds_prefix_holdout.csv` — the fold protocol, one row per clean train volume (195). Fold A tunes on the `6bba` family (n=126) and evaluates on `44b6` (n=69); fold B reverses. The four public-test twin volumes are already excluded from these tables (195 clean = 199 minus the 4 twins); the is_public_test_twin column is retained for anyone rebuilding with twins included.
- `gt_per_volume_stats.csv` — per-volume ground-truth statistics for all 195 volumes: annotated nodes/edges, metadata node-count estimate (`est`), frames spanned, nodes-per-frame level/dispersion/trend, division counts, and frame-to-frame displacement percentiles (`disp_med/p95/p99/max`, in anisotropy-scaled units, scale (1.625, 0.40625, 0.40625)). Use `disp_p99` for gating radii and `est` for node budgets.
- `fork162_per_volume_run_stats.csv` — per-volume pipeline telemetry (78 columns: node/edge counts, edge-to-node ratio, division-like sources, gap-closing and relink counters) from our measurement run of a recovered public 0.916-targeting fork variant across the same 195 volumes. Useful as a calibration reference for what a 0.915-class pipeline emits per volume.
- `public_leaderboard_2026-08-20.csv` — full 2,580-row public leaderboard snapshot (2026-08-20T20:16Z, Kaggle CLI): Rank, TeamId, TeamName, LastSubmissionDate, Score, SubmissionCount, TeamMemberUserNames.
- `leaderboard_timeline.csv` — dated reads of the 0.915 block's decay: a frozen fork entry fell rank 360 → 531 between 2026-08-19 and 2026-08-20 while its score never moved, and the bronze-line display crossed 0.916 → 0.917.
- `score.py`, `eval_setup.py`, `control.py` — the local scoring harness. Runs inside a Kaggle kernel with the competition attached: it locates the competition's own `tracking_cellmot` scorer under `/kaggle/input`, builds the prediction graph per volume, and reports per-volume and fold-level scores. `control.py` re-scores an unchanged reference alongside any candidate; require control drift 0.000000 before believing a delta.
- `build_pack.py` — deterministic builder for the derived CSVs in this pack.

## Method / provenance

All statistics were computed by us from the competition's train split (195 clean volumes; the 4 public twins excluded from every evaluation) using the fixed prefix-holdout protocol above, on the competition's own scorer. The fork telemetry comes from executing a publicly shared pipeline variant (pilkwang-lineage artifacts; the plain 0.915 fork's upstream source is no longer retrievable) through the same harness. Leaderboard files are unmodified Kaggle CLI downloads. Nothing here contains competition image data — only derived statistics, fold definitions, code, and public leaderboard records. Reference points measured with this exact harness: an honest from-scratch lane at CV 0.548526 scored 0.595 public; confirmed-on-both-folds steps included per-volume budget plus edgeless-node pruning (fold A 0.471149 -> 0.501604, fold B 0.495111 -> 0.580255) and sub-voxel refinement (CV 0.540929 -> 0.548526).

## Mount and use

```python
import pandas as pd
folds = pd.read_csv('/kaggle/input/biohub-local-cv-pack/folds_prefix_holdout.csv')
gt = pd.read_csv('/kaggle/input/biohub-local-cv-pack/gt_per_volume_stats.csv')
eval_A = folds[folds.fold_A_role == 'evaluate'].volume  # twins are already excluded from these tables
```

Companion notebook (walkthrough + what actually moves the metric): "Bronze moved to 0.917 — your 0.915 is sinking".

## Limitations

Ground-truth annotations in this competition are sparse, so `nodes` counts annotated cells, not all cells (`est` is the volume-metadata estimate of the full count). The fork telemetry describes one recovered variant, not the exact plain-0.915 checkpoint. Leaderboard files are point-in-time snapshots; re-pull for current standings.

## License and credit

CC0-1.0 for everything in this pack. The scorer it wraps (`tracking_cellmot`) ships with the competition and stays there — this pack contains only our wrapper code. Credit to `inversion`'s nearest-neighbor getting-started notebook, `pilkwang`'s public model/support artifacts, and `yusuketogashi`'s no-hack local-CV line for the public groundwork this builds on.
